ACCESSIBLE MEDIA TRANSCRIPT

One design question.
Two gap hypotheses.

The 36-second video uses six still captures of the actual application. Each remains visible for six seconds. It has no audio. The pauses are editorial timing, not solver latency or continuous screen recording.

0 to 6 seconds

Board explorer asks whether adding solder would help an actual ULX3S U1/J16 joint. The source lower copper is 400 µm. Other joints supply context and remain unsolved. The explicit worked-example action preserves one prior input snapshot for restoration.

6 to 12 seconds

The process assumptions show a 400 µm upper pad, 300 µm held gap, +240 µm offset, and 40 versus 56 nL liquid volume. Surface tension is 0.48 N/m, density is 9 g/cm³, and gravity is enabled. The board identifies lower copper, not these hypothetical assembly conditions.

12 to 18 seconds

The 300 µm comparison shows X/Z forces of −184.526/−181.284 µN for 40 nL and −164.385/+13.386 µN for 56 nL. Only 40 nL meets the numerical held-gap fixture rule of lateral restoration without upward separation. Physical force accuracy remains unqualified.

18 to 24 seconds

The 330 µm trial changes only held gap. The X/Z forces become −169.063/−227.390 µN for 40 nL and −170.455/−82.276 µN for 56 nL. Both now meet the same numerical rule. Two sampled hypotheses do not establish manufacturing tolerance, physical accuracy or a production choice.

24 to 30 seconds

The expanded candidate result shows its current inputs and numerical status. The result belongs to that exact input snapshot. Editing an assumption clears the current result and export links. Readable review, editable case and board-bound evidence preserve distinct parts of the comparison. A verified recording is labeled separately from fresh computation.

30 to 36 seconds

The matching Physical test handoff identifies the hot boundaries, liquid volume, geometry, material and force measurements still required. The existing 200 µm fixture needs adaptation for the 400 µm joint. The separate 220 versus 270 µm clearance coupon has a 185 µm target and cannot validate these forces.
